intro.text: One of several strange figures, invisible to others, that Shallan Davar finds she has unconsciously sketched into her drawings in Kharbranth.
A spren of the kind that call themselves Cryptics, bonded to Shallan Davar. In the Physical Realm he appears as a shifting raised pattern, and at first he is almost mindless.
Pattern, a Cryptic bonded to Shallan Davar. His true name is a string of numbers, so she named him Pattern while studying him on Jasnah's orders.
Pattern is the Cryptic bonded to Shallan Davar, granting her the Surges of Illumination and Transformation. Their bond has grown strong enough for him to become her Shardblade.

story.text: While sketching King Taravangian in Kharbranth, Shallan unknowingly drew several strange figures who had been standing in the room, unseen by everyone there. They had somehow been caught in the Memory she used to draw.

Some weeks afterward, as Shallan puzzled over the Soulcaster alone in her room, the spren spoke to her, seeking a new truth. Alarmed by the bodiless voice, she told herself it was only the maid cleaning next door.

When Shallan sketched the ardent Kabsal, the strange figures appeared in her drawing again. She fled in a panic, drawing scenes to track them, and they followed her to her room, where she accidentally Soulcast a goblet into blood and hid it by cutting her own arm.

The figures kept following Shallan in the hospital, whispering to her. When she confronted Jasnah about the Soulcaster, Shallan called on them, confessing that she had killed her father; the truth was accepted and she was pulled into the Cognitive Realm, nearly drowning in a sea of glass beads before Jasnah brought her back.

Once Shallan spoke her truths, the spren bonded her and crossed into the Physical Realm, losing much of his mind. Aboard ship he appeared as a raised pattern on her sketchpad and on a wave, vanishing whenever she looked. When she finally captured him in a Memory and sketched him, he settled in, behaving like a curious animal or small child.

Jasnah explained that the symbol-headed spren from Kharbranth called themselves Cryptics, disliked the human name liespren, and seemed to rule at least one great city in the Cognitive Realm. She told a disappointed Shallan to study the childlike spren closely, since she was likely the first in centuries with the chance.

The spren ignored Shallan's wish to keep him hidden and unsettled the sailors. He was horrified to learn that eating destroyed food, yet grasped abstract ideas quickly, especially truth and lies, praising the sailor Yalb's lies as good ones because they were rooted in truth. Talk of memory stirred an old memory in Shallan, and she unintentionally turned part of the deck green before forcing it away.

When assassins attacked the ship and stabbed Jasnah, the spren helped Shallan create an illusion of herself that led them overboard. To save the crew, she had him help her Soulcast the ship; in the Cognitive Realm she saw him as a symbol-headed figure, and he translated as she persuaded the ship to become water.

The spren and Shallan survived the sinking. Ashore, he found one of Jasnah's trunks and excitedly led Shallan to it. He again translated when she failed to Soulcast a stick into fire, anxious at being near the Cognitive Realm. The pair then came upon the slaver Tvlakv, whom Shallan persuaded to take her to the Shattered Plains.

Shallan named the spren Pattern, since his real name was a string of numbers. Hidden in Jasnah's trunk, he asked why she was going on to the Shattered Plains, and recalled that the Cryptics, fearing the Desolations, had sent him to her because of her lies. When she found an old drawing of Jasnah and broke down, he comforted her.

Pattern spied on Tvlakv for Shallan, learning the slaver hoped to hold her for ransom. As she learned to draw in Stormlight, he admitted he was a scholar sent to study her, and that he expected her to kill him, something he linked to the Knights Radiant of old.

When the deserter Vathah angrily confronted Shallan, Pattern hid on the back of his uniform and spoke calmly to him, leaving the man thinking he was hearing voices, while Shallan pretended not to notice.

Highstorms agitated Pattern, who buzzed and ranted, unnerving the people sheltering with Shallan. He argued that truth depends on a person's experience, and reluctantly named Odium as a third influence on spren. The next storm felt wrong to him and filled him with fear.

When Tyn, who had been hired to assassinate Jasnah, learned who Shallan was and attacked her, Pattern imitated Jasnah's voice to distract her, then fetched Vathah and his men to help. Shallan killed Tyn.

Pattern unlocked Tyn's chest so Shallan could dress for meeting Dalinar Kholin, and rode along blending into her clothing. In Sebarial's mansion he puzzled over taste, and noticed that the messages on Tyn's spanreed contained a code used to confirm the writer's identity.

Warned by Pattern about the code, Shallan posed as Tyn over the spanreed and met the group Tyn worked for, disguised as Veil, with Pattern watching for anyone following her. Afterward he spotted a woman tailing her, innocently asked if they were now friends, and checked when it was safe after Shallan hid.

Pattern decoded some Dawnchant from the city names on Shallan's maps and discussed finding a way to Urithiru. He accompanied her, hidden, on her date with Adolin. The next night, he unlocked Amaram's secret room for her and supplied Amaram's voice while she provided his image.

After a Ghostblood meeting, Pattern imitated Shallan's voice to send her coach back while she hid inside an illusory boulder. On the way back they found the coach burned and its driver dead, proving her caution right. Pattern also helped her practice accents by repeating her voice.

During Adolin's duel against four Shardbearers, Pattern distracted Abrobadar and drew Syl's attention before fleeing. Shallan then found that he could hold her illusions crisp when she was away, and that illusions anchored to him could move and draw Stormlight.

Anchored to an image of Veil, Pattern retrieved instructions left by Tyn's former employers and distracted a watcher while Shallan got them into Dalinar's monastery. He found the madman Shallan had been sent to locate and unlocked his door, though the man reacted violently when she drew in Stormlight.

After Shallan and Kaladin survived the chasms, Pattern spied on Dalinar and Navani discussing whether she should join the expedition onto the Plains. He could not tell her whether she was Radiant enough to work an Oathgate, explaining that the deaths of spren in the Recreance had left gaps in what they knew.

On the expedition, Pattern helped Shallan sort fact from fiction in Words of Radiance. He dismissed creationspren as purposeless, and was fascinated by the story of the artist Eleseth for what it showed about how humans ignore lies.

Buzzing at the coming storm, Pattern revealed himself to Shallan's fellow scholars, who feared he was linked to the Voidbringers; he denied it. He warned that the highstorm and Everstorm would clash, and urged Shallan to view the Oathgate in a wider context. She realized it was a fabrial and activated it, carrying the army to Urithiru.

In Urithiru, Pattern arranged for Shallan a room that resembled her father's study, and pushed her to admit the truth of her mother's death and her own part in it, including the Shardblade she had used that night. Pattern accepted that she hated him and would one day kill him for it; she replied that she wanted only her family back.

Pattern tried to tell Shallan he understood why she hated him. Not wanting him to understand, she began separating her spren from the Shardblade in her mind, insisting she hated the sword, not him, which only confused him.

Shallan formally introduced Pattern to Adolin, who named him chaperone for the evening. Once he understood the role, he cheerfully reminded them of his presence when they kissed. When Adolin offered to teach Shallan the Shardblade, Pattern approved, and offered to die and be replaced if she wished; instead she created the persona Brightness Radiant to wield him calmly.

Exploring Urithiru's depths, Shallan wove the tale of The Girl Who Looked Up for Pattern in an old theater, and they failed to notice an Unmade hiding in the illusory audience. They chased it into the ventilation shafts; Pattern remembered little of the creature but knew it came from Odium.

After the creature killed again, Pattern and Shallan chased it until it slipped through a hole. Shallan cut through the wall to find a hidden passage, and Pattern fetched Adolin, Renarin and men of Bridge Four. Below, the Unmade tried to tear away Shallan's bond and replace Pattern; she clung to him, and it fled.

Pattern sensed memories held in a hidden gem archive in the tower's libraries, and spotted lies in a Ghostblood note about Shallan's brother Helaran. Renarin found he could see Pattern, who cannot turn invisible, and when Jasnah infused one of the archive's gems, Pattern noticed its vibrations formed a code.

In besieged Kholinar, Pattern drew guards away when Shallan's attempt to enter the palace went wrong, then fetched Kaladin. He distracted guards with sound while Shallan and Vathah stole food from Nananav, mimicked the whispers of the Cult of Moments' Unmade so Shallan could explore, and reminded her of the other children she fed after Grund was killed.

Shallan fought the Unmade on the Oathgate platform with Pattern as her Blade, and it withdrew. As the city fell, she activated the Oathgate, but those in the control room were sent into Shadesmar, where Pattern, Syl and Maya took their Cognitive forms.

In Shadesmar, Pattern tested Shallan's manifested platforms across the beads and steadied her, keeping watch while the others slept. He discussed the nature of spren with Syl, loomed unnervingly over negotiations with Riino, and in Celebrant translated as the group searched for a ship and hid from the Fused.

Aboard Honor's Path, Pattern and his companions were locked up by the honorspren until Fused pursuit forced them to flee into the beads. He found Shallan and Kaladin in a pocket she had made, and stayed by her as they crossed the sea toward Thaylenah.

At the Thaylen Oathgate, Pattern mingled with Shallan's illusions, slashing at the air to confuse the Fused guards, then helped pull the wounded Adolin to safety. Though puzzled by Shallan's behavior toward Kaladin afterward, he agreed with her choice to stay engaged to Adolin.

About a year after Thaylen Field, Pattern kept watch as Shallan went undercover among the Sons of Honor. When she was moved, she briefly began summoning him as a Blade to signal her location, which he passed on to Adolin. When Veil confronted Ialai Sadeas, he cheerfully reported that Adolin was almost there.

After Ialai's death, Pattern found a repeating pattern of glyph-marked stones in her chambers, one showing a map of Shinovar, which led Shallan to a hidden notebook of Ialai's notes on the Ghostbloods. Riding away, he hummed as Shallan rested against Adolin.

At Jez's Duty with Veil, Adolin and Kaladin, Pattern wondered aloud how human babies were born and agreed that Shallan was struggling; Kaladin suggested he ask Wit for help. The next morning he danced among creationspren as Shallan drew an idealized picture of her family.

In Shadesmar, Pattern and three other Cryptics crowded Shallan as she drew, triggering a panic that made her become Radiant. Pattern apologized, explaining that he was famous among Cryptics for studying humans, and told her Cryptics can lie, though badly, and that everything is math.

Shallan noticed her communication cube had been moved and warned each Lightweaver of a different corrupted spren to trap the spy. Pattern overheard her warning to Beryl about gloryspren. When Mraize repeated that warning, Shallan suspected Beryl; Pattern told her truthfully that he had not seen Beryl use the cube, and said he and Adolin were worried about her.

Left to guard camp on the way to Lasting Integrity, Pattern secretly used the cube to reach Wit, who said a Ghostblood was spying on him. Veil had dusted the cube with powder and found it disturbed. When she tested Pattern with an invented memory, he claimed to remember it, and his mention of corrupted gloryspren convinced Shallan he was the spy.

Pattern explained that his attempts to help Shallan remember her past had hurt her, so he had decided lying was best, and saw now that it was not working. He told Radiant he had bonded Shallan, despite expecting it to kill him, to see the Physical Realm and because humans and spren had to unite against Odium.

Abandoning a task Veil had given him, Pattern admitted he had lied and used the cube, and brought another Cryptic to meet Shallan. She refused and ignored the visitor. Pattern sensed her personality had changed, and kept asking whether she was really Veil.

Earlier, Pattern had gone alone to Wit for help with Shallan's worsening mental health; Wit got him a key to her trunk and suggested contacting him through Mraize's cube. Now Pattern knelt, took Shallan's hands and told her the truth: none of her friends were spying for Mraize. Veil asked him to keep no more secrets, and he agreed.

Pattern was delighted by the irony when Mraize revealed that the Sons of Honor, devoted to restoring the Heralds, were secretly led by one. At Adolin's trial, he helped Shallan con the honorspren into thinking she would die without Stormlight, and thanked Veil for letting him lie.

On the last day of the trial, as Shallan prepared to assassinate Kalak, Pattern warned her against it and followed her, repeating Wit's message that she deserved trust and love, and apologizing for lying. His words set off a dialogue among Shallan's personas that let her recover her buried memories of her first spren and integrate Veil.

Pattern decoded a note Mraize had left with a metal cube. After the trial, he helped Shallan choose an Alethi name for her first Cryptic, and hummed beside that Cryptic as Shallan told Mraize she was leaving the Ghostbloods.

personality.text: Though he can blend in silently, Pattern tends to buzz or hum audibly when excited or anxious, which unnerves people who cannot tell where the sound comes from.

In the Physical Realm, Pattern usually appears as a complex, constantly shifting geometric pattern raised slightly off a surface, or sometimes as a floating knot of twisting lines. He cannot become fully invisible but blends into surfaces so that only those looking for him notice.

Pattern is fascinated by things that mix truth and falsehood, such as flattery, sarcasm and metaphor, admiringly calling them lies. Human languages and customs puzzle him with their inconsistencies, and he often takes words like 'odd' or 'mean' in their mathematical sense.

In the Cognitive Realm, Pattern is tall and willowy, wearing a stiff robe, with a head made of an ever-shifting pattern of sharp lines and impossible geometry that speeds up when he is excited and slows or wilts when he is upset.

Pattern is usually perky, enthusiastic and inquisitive, bouncing as he walks where other Cryptics glide, but grows serious when Shallan's well-being is at stake. Studying humans and then bonding Shallan show his courage and willingness to risk his life for others.
